title: Apigenin attenuates MASLD progression by suppressing lipogenesis and macrophage M1-like inflammatory activation: involvement of SMAD4-associated signaling.
authors: Cao, Lijun; Zhao, Yongna; Li, Ping
one_liner_zh: 该文研究芹菜素通过SMAD4信号改善MASLD的脂质合成与炎症，仅用分子对接预测小分子-蛋白互作，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，且无AI或物理模拟方法，与本课题关联极弱。
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is characterized by dysregulated hepatic lipid metabolism and persistent inflammatory remodeling. Apigenin has lipid-regulatory and anti-inflammatory activities, but the molecular basis linking these effects remains incompletely understood. This study investigated whether SMAD4-associated signaling contributes to the coordinated regulation of hepatocyte lipogenesis and macrophage inflammatory activation by apigenin. C57BL/6J mice were fed a high-fat diet (HFD) to establish MASLD and treated with apigenin. Palmitic acid (PA)-treated HepG2 cells and lipopolysaccharide (LPS)-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages were used as complementary in vitro models. Hepatic lipid accumulation, inflammatory responses, macrophage phenotype, and SMAD4-associated signaling were evaluated using biochemical assays, histological staining, ELISA, RT-qPCR, Western blotting, immunohistochemistry, and immunofluorescence. Molecular docking was used to predict the potential interaction between apigenin and SMAD4, a cellular thermal shift assay (CETSA) was performed in HepG2 cells to assess cellular target engagement of SMAD4 by apigenin, and SMAD4/Smad4 overexpression was used to evaluate functional involvement. Apigenin alleviated HFD-induced liver injury, dyslipidemia, and hepatic lipid deposition and suppressed the SREBP-1c/FAS/ACC lipogenic program in mouse liver and PA-treated HepG2 cells. Apigenin also reduced hepatic CD68-positive macrophage accumulation, decreased CD86 and iNOS expression and pro-inflammatory cytokine levels, and attenuated M1-like inflammatory activation in vivo and in LPS-stimulated RAW264.7 macrophages. Molecular docking predicted a favorable interaction between apigenin and SMAD4, while CETSA demonstrated increased thermal stability of SMAD4 following apigenin exposure in HepG2 cells, supporting cellular target engagement in this cellular context. Apigenin further attenuated SMAD4-associated signaling, whereas SMAD4/Smad4 overexpression partially counteracted its anti-lipogenic and anti-inflammatory effects in HepG2 cells and RAW264.7 macrophages, respectively. These findings indicate that apigenin alleviates HFD-induced MASLD by coordinately suppressing hepatocellular lipogenesis and macrophage-associated inflammatory activation and suggest that SMAD4-associated signaling contributes to these metabolic and inflammatory effects.
abstract_zh: 代谢功能障碍相关脂肪性肝病（MASLD）以肝脏脂质代谢失调和持续性炎症重塑为特征。芹菜素具有调脂和抗炎活性，但连接这些效应的分子基础尚未完全阐明。本研究探讨了SMAD4相关信号是否参与芹菜素对肝细胞脂质生成和巨噬细胞炎症激活的协同调控。C57BL/6J小鼠被喂食高脂饮食（HFD）以建立MASLD模型，并给予芹菜素处理。棕榈酸（PA）处理的HepG2细胞和脂多糖（LPS）刺激的RAW264.7巨噬细胞作为互补的体外模型。通过生化检测、组织学染色、ELISA、RT-qPCR、Western blotting、免疫组织化学和免疫荧光评估肝脏脂质积累、炎症反应、巨噬细胞表型及SMAD4相关信号。分子对接用于预测芹菜素与SMAD4之间的潜在相互作用，在HepG2细胞中进行细胞热位移分析（CETSA）以评估芹菜素对SMAD4的细胞靶点结合，并通过SMAD4/Smad4过表达评估其功能参与。芹菜素减轻了HFD诱导的肝损伤、血脂异常和肝脏脂质沉积，并抑制了小鼠肝脏和PA处理的HepG2细胞中SREBP-1c/FAS/ACC脂质生成程序。芹菜素还减少了肝脏CD68阳性巨噬细胞积累，降低了CD86和iNOS表达及促炎细胞因子水平，并在体内和LPS刺激的RAW264.7巨噬细胞中减弱了M1样炎症激活。分子对接预测了芹菜素与SMAD4之间的有利相互作用，而CETSA表明在HepG2细胞中芹菜素暴露后SMAD4的热稳定性增加，支持了该细胞环境中的细胞靶点结合。芹菜素进一步减弱了SMAD4相关信号，而SMAD4/Smad4过表达分别部分抵消了其在HepG2细胞和RAW264.7巨噬细胞中的抗脂质生成和抗炎效应。这些发现表明，芹菜素通过协同抑制肝细胞脂质生成和巨噬细胞相关炎症激活来缓解HFD诱导的MASLD，并提示SMAD4相关信号有助于这些代谢和炎症效应。
